waterbody.name: Boac River
waterbody.identityBasis: exact GBIF locality text only; no independent waterbody geometry crosswalk reviewed

question: Does GBIF's occurrence index provide exact-locality fish records for Boac River that could independently support a fish occurrence claim?

queryReview.method: Read-only country=PH searches of exact waterBody and locality strings. A separate classKey query used the GBIF backbone key for Actinopterygii. Search responses were limited to five records; all three exact-locality records were reviewed via the single-record API. No bulk download was requested.

dataset.title: UF Invertebrate Zoology
dataset.citation: Florida Museum of Natural History: UF Invertebrate Zoology, GBIF dataset DOI 10.15468/sm6qo6.

queryReview.recordHandling: The exact-locality records are preserved specimens identified by GBIF as Gastropoda, not fish. Their returned occurrence records contain no eventDate, year, or coordinates. Record identifiers and non-sensitive citation metadata are retained; no occurrence payload or coordinate data was copied into app datasets.

interpretation.result: The GBIF index returned three specimen records with locality exactly 'Boac River'; all three are gastropods. The exact-locality Actinopterygii query returned zero indexed records.
interpretation.scope: This is a text-field screen of records indexed by GBIF as of 2026-11-06. It is not a river survey and does not establish fish presence or absence in Boac River.
interpretation.taxonomicUse: The three indexed records do not support a Bangwit fish-species entry. No fish taxonomy, waterbody occurrence, diet, catchability, safety, or legal claim is inferred.

limitations: Exact waterBody/locality searches can miss alternate spellings, absent or inconsistent Darwin Core fields, unindexed collections, records outside GBIF, and specimens whose collection site was not transcribed.
A zero-result class-filtered index query is not evidence that Actinopterygii are absent from the river.
The specimen locality string was not independently reconciled to a mapped river reach; the records have no coordinates, event dates, or years in the GBIF responses reviewed.
The records are gastropods and do not constitute fish-survey coverage; their exact locality labels alone do not establish a habitat-specific ecological relationship.
The dataset and occurrence records state CC BY-NC 4.0. This screen does not add any occurrence to Bangwit's public app data or establish permission for commercial reuse.

followUp.nextAction: Continue MIMAROPA discovery with an independently documented inland fish survey or specimen-backed dataset for a named river, lake, wetland, or reservoir. Revisit Boac River if a site-specific fish baseline or other dated fish collection becomes accessible.
